name: Schlitters
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful residential community in the lower Zillertal with a natural swimming pond and beautiful location along the Ziller.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Schlitters is situated in the Schwaz district at the entrance to the Zillertal valley at an altitude of 548 metres on the eastern bank of the Ziller River, home to around 1,550 residents. The village rests on the broad alluvial cone of the Öxlbach stream flowing from the Kellerjoch massif. Known as the welcoming Gateway to the Zillertal, Schlitters unites peaceful rural ambience with immediate proximity to world-class ski domains and Inntal cultural attractions. A pristine natural bathing lake, the cascading Schlitters Waterfall, and level cycling routes establish Schlitters as a cherished holiday haven for families and outdoor recreationists.

Geschichte

The name Schlitters traces back to pre-Roman roots, denoting ancient settlement. The community was first documented in 931 AD as Slitteres when Archbishop Adalbert of Salzburg granted local tithes to a vassal. In the 12th century, the noble Knights of Schlitters maintained a fortified seat overlooking the valley. Between the 15th and 17th centuries, copper and silver mining flourished in adjacent mountain ravines. Emperor Maximilian I established a princely fish pond here to breed char and trout for the imperial court in Innsbruck, representing the historical foundation of today's bathing lake. The Late Gothic parish church of Saint Martin was built between 1500 and 1505 and baroquised around 1740, featuring a monumental 1940 Saint Christopher fresco by Hans Andre on its exterior wall.

Anreise

Transport connections to Schlitters are exceptionally swift. Motorists leave the Inntalautobahn A12 at exit Wiesing/Zillertal, traverse the Brettfall Tunnel along the B169 Zillertalstraße, and reach the Schlitters exit in under five minutes. Rail passengers travel on ÖBB or DB express trains to Jenbach junction and transfer onto the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn. Trains run every half hour, stopping at the Schlitters-Bruck station at the edge of the village. Furthermore, VVT regional bus line 8330 runs continuously, and the paved Zillertal-Radweg cycle trail passes directly by.

Tipps

A favourite summer retreat is Lake Schlitters (Badesee Schlitters), an idyllic swimming lake set amidst lush greenery with sunbathing lawns, a lakeside restaurant, and an adventure woodland playground featuring wooden suspension bridges. Nature enthusiasts can walk in thirty minutes through the shaded Öxlbach gorge to the rushing Schlitters Waterfall, enjoying cool mountain spray. Cyclists can follow the paved, traffic-free Zillertal-Radweg trail following the riverbanks. Within a five-minute drive, visitors reach the Spieljochbahn cable car in Fügen, while the Hochzillertal ski arena in Kaltenbach is reached in ten minutes.
